header:
Date: 2026-11-02 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 min
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Nguyen (Redwood Solutions Eng); Ethan Rivera (CTO, HorizonPay), Priya Shah (Head of MLOps), Sam Osei (Infra)
summary: Discovery call focused on Dedicated capacity: reserved GPUs, isolation requirements, burst strategy, scaling expectations, and security/compliance checks. HorizonPay is evaluating dedicated vs hosted for production fraud-detection pipelines; interested in cost predictability and strict data isolation (PCI scope). Action items: pricing, security docs, infra workshop, pilot benchmarking.
topics: current infra and constraints; why Dedicated vs Hosted; GPU sizing and burst model; autoscaling and prediction of traffic; SLOs (latency/throughput); quantization and batching tradeoffs; network isolation, VPC peering, KMS; rollout/canary plans and fallback to hosted; pricing and contract model; next steps and pilot plan
transcript:
15:00 Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we really appreciate you taking the time. this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm joined by Maya and Carlos from our SE/solutions engineering team. can you start with quick intros?
15:06 Ethan: Yeah thanks Jordan, Ethan Rivera here, CTO at HorizonPay. Priya Shah our head of MLOps and Sam Osei who owns infra. really interested in dedicated capacity for our fraud detection model, got some concerns around PCI scope and latency.
15:12 Priya: hi all, brief context — we run a streaming scoring pipeline, about 200 to 2k requests per second depending on time of day, tail latency needs to be sub-200ms for most requests, and some batched heavy jobs for nightly re-scores. We're evaluating hosted vs dedicated because of data isolation + predictable cost.
15:28 Jordan: got it, thanks. high-level, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, private network options, and contract-backed SLAs. Maya, do you want to walk through the capacity and burst model?
15:35 Maya: yeah sure. so with Dedicated you reserve N GPU cards — we typically size by RPS and model throughput. we also support burst capacity for short spikes; bursts can be routed from your dedicated pool to either reserved burst nodes in our infra or to a compatible hosted variant depending on policy. that keeps your steady cost predictable but allows handling traffic peaks.
15:51 Sam: question — when you say "compatible hosted variant" does that mean data may leave our VPC? We need to remain within our PCI boundary.
15:58 Maya: good q. for Private/Dedicated in a VPC deployment we offer full network isolation and you can choose no egress; for Redwood Dedicated (managed) we can configure VPC peering so traffic stays over private links. the hosted fallback option is opt-in and we can enforce that fallback not be used for PCI-scoped requests. there are tradeoffs though for availability on extreme spikes.
16:15 Ethan: so we need a plan where anything PCI hits a strictly isolated path, and non-PCI can use burst. is that supported?
16:22 Carlos: yes, you can route by policy — for example: requests tagged PCI go to the dedicated pool only; non-PCI can use burst. We have routing rules and headers-based routing. small caveat: if you cannot allow any egress at all, then bursts must be from pre-provisioned reserved burst capacity within your Dedicated contract.
16:38 Priya: rough numbers, our 99th percentile request token length is small, but some requests spike; how do you size GPUs? what's the per-GPU qps for typical LLMs?
16:47 Maya: depends on model and quantization; for a Llama 2 style 7B quantized to int8 we might get X tokens/sec and Y requests/sec — sorry i'm saying generic. practical sizing: we recommend starting with 4-8 A100-class GPUs for low-latency production, with autoscaling policies that add or remove nodes in minutes. for heavier LLMs 16+ GPUs. We will run benchmarks with your prompts to get concrete numbers.
17:08 Sam: autoscaling in Dedicated — is it automatic or manual? how quick is scale up?
17:12 Maya: Dedicated supports configured autoscale policies. scale-up latency is a function of pre-warmed capacity: if you reserve extra burst nodes they can come online in under a minute; if we have to provision new nodes from the pool it can be several minutes. We also support instant routing to hot standby nodes if pre-warmed.
17:29 Ethan: latency targets — we need p95 under 150ms ideally. can you hit that for our model?
17:34 Maya: we'll need to benchmark but typical sub-150ms p95 is achievable with proper batching and KV-cache priming for short-context models; long context or heavy decoding will push latency. Also quantization and optimized kernels matter.
17:49 Priya: what about batching — we need low latency so large batching is bad; how do you balance cost vs latency?
17:55 Carlos: we have continuous batching that is workload-aware; you can set latency SLOs and the runtime will favor smaller batches for low tail latency and opportunistically batch when it doesn't violate SLOs. that's a key levers for cost.
18:10 Ethan: security — SOC2, SSO, audit logs, KMS?
18:14 Jordan: yes, we are SOC2 compliant, we have SSO/SAML and RBAC, and KMS integrations for key management. Maya will share our security pack; we also provide audit logs per request and token-level cost tracing.
18:25 Sam: network details — we run in AWS us-east-1, need VPC peering and specific outbound IPs for allowlists.
18:30 Maya: we can do VPC peering, PrivateLink, or customer-managed VPC depending on the Private/Dedicated flavor. we'll include a network diagram. outbound IPs can be provided for allowlisting.
18:40 Priya: interested in fallback/canary strategy — we want canary deploys and automatic fallback to older model on regressions.
18:46 Carlos: supported — our rollout features allow canary percentages, A/B, and automated rollback based on configurable quality or latency metrics. you can also pin traffic to a version.
18:55 Ethan: what about model updates — how do we handle model versioning and KV cache warmup?
18:59 Maya: we offer model pinning and staged rollouts. for KV cache warmup we can pre-warm with a priming set; we recommend a short warmup window in the canary to populate caches.
19:12 Priya: cost predictability — can you give an example contract? we're trying to compare dedicated commit vs hosted usage math.
19:17 Jordan: sure, typical Dedicated reserved contract is monthly commit by GPU count. burst nodes can be included as a small % of the commit or as on-demand at higher unit cost. I'll send a sample pricing sheet showing per-GPU price, burst rates, and egress/network costs.
19:33 Ethan: competitors question — some of our teams looked at InferMax and CloudEndor, and our platform team also considered self-hosting. why Redwood vs them?
19:41 Jordan: good q; quick differentiators — we focus on production economics and observability: token-level cost breakdowns, built-in routing and quality rollback features, and unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private. we also have strong kernel/runtime optimizations and recommendations for quantization. I'll include benchmark examples.
19:55 Sam: operationally who owns the infra for Dedicated? is Redwood managing nodes or are they customer-managed?
20:01 Maya: two flavors: Managed Dedicated where Redwood owns and operates the GPU pool with VPC peering and SLAs; and Private where you run on your infra or a customer-managed VPC with our control plane. Managed reduces ops burden; Private gives max control.
20:15 Priya: for PCI we likely need Private or Managed Dedicated with strict no-egress options to meet audit. We need KMS customer managed keys as well.
20:23 Jordan: understood. we support customer KMS in Private and can work with dedicated managed to integrate your KMS for encryption.
20:30 Ethan: timeline — we want to be in pilot by mid-November and production by Jan. Is that realistic?
20:36 Maya: yes, pilot in 2 weeks is doable if we get prompt sets and access for benchmarking. production by January is feasible with a Dedicated contract and standard rollout.
20:46 Jordan: recap — Jordan sends pricing and sample contract; Maya sends security + network docs and we'll schedule infra workshop; Priya provides prompts and throughput targets; Sam confirms VPC details. we'll plan pilot benchmark for a 3-day window.
20:58 Priya: sounds good. one more thing — people sometimes see transcription issues in these notes so we'll follow up with the docs.
21:04 Ethan: thanks everyone, this was helpful. we'll meet again after the infra workshop.
21:07 Jordan: thanks all, talk soon.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts (proper nouns may be slightly off), speakers labeled by name but some audio overlap. attachments referenced: link to pricing sheet (deck), security-pack.pdf, network-diagram.png, benchmark-template.csv
